key_insight: Direct light-driven charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbed CO is strongly material-dependent, with electron injection dominating because the CO LUMO lies closer to the metal Fermi level than the HOMO.
engineering_relevance: The results provide design guidance for choosing nanoparticle metals that maximize photocatalytic charge transfer efficiency for specific surface reactions.
method: Combined ab initio density functional theory for adsorbate–metal interactions with a macroscopic electrodynamics model of localized surface plasmons.
Computed hot-electron and hot-hole injection rates for large spherical nanoparticles.
Compared nine metals spanning plasmonic, emerging plasmonic, and non-plasmonic candidates.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates predicted injection rates across nine metals and finds the largest optical-range electron injection for Al, Ag, Cu, and Au, with Cu and Au showing strong plasmonic enhancement.
watch_item: The results are specific to spherical nanoparticles and CO adsorption, so performance may differ for other shapes, adsorbates, or surface chemistries.
paper_title: Material dependence of direct light-induced charge injection from metallic nanoparticles into adsorbates
